LESSON: PRODUCT PROCESSING AND VALUE ADDITION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Agricultural Technologies and Entrepreneurship
Topic 3.2: Product Processing and Value Addition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Product Processing and Value Addition, part of Agricultural Technologies and Entrepreneurship in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How does value addition enhance nutrition and food security? 2. How does value addition benefit rural economies and smallholder farmers?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Product Processing and Value Addition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Responsibility: learner takes care of other learners’ items and products when undertaking a project on value addition

of agricultural produce.

● Peace: learner co-exists harmoniously when undertaking project tasks on selected value addition processes and

making exhibitions of value-added products.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Life skills: learner demonstrates peaceful conflict management skills when carrying out a project on selected value

addition processes.

● Consumer education: learner develops consumer awareness when discussing and presenting ethical concerns in

processing and value addition of agricultural produce to protect consumers or users.

Suggested learning resources

• Digital devices with assistive technology

• Print materials

• Braille materials

• Photographs of unprocessed and processed agricultural produce of plant origin and animal origin

• Crop and animal produce to be processed such as milk, honey, hides and vegetable produce such as fruits

• Source of heat,

• Kitchen tools and equipment (sieves, sufurias, knives, cooking spoon, chopping board)

Suggested Key Skills

● Carry out processing of agricultural produce of plant and animal origin.

● Carry out home-based packaging and branding of processed agricultural products.

● Design innovative value addition equipment for agricultural produce.
